reason: The Baptist Faith and Message 2000 contains no mention of alcohol, drinking, drunkenness, temperance or abstinence anywhere in its eighteen articles; Article XV (Christian and the Social Order) addresses racism, sexual immorality, the unborn and social order, but not alcohol, and no other article touches the subject.

Article I addresses Scripture's inspiration, truthfulness and authority only. It says nothing about providence, reason, or the ordinary means of guidance, and does not address or exclude an inward impression as a channel of guidance.

Article III grounds the image of God in inherent human dignity and personhood (“the sacredness of human personality is evident in that God created man in His own image”), not in a vocation of dominion or rule over creation; it teaches no functional/dominion reading of the image.

citation: Baptist Faith and Message (2000), Article III
note: The confession says: “The sacredness of human personality is evident in that God created man in His own image, and in that Christ died for man; therefore, every person of every race possesses full dignity and is worthy of respect and Christian love.”

reason: The Baptist Faith and Message 2000 contains no statement anywhere about the intermediate state; Article X moves directly from bodily death and resurrection to final judgment and eternal destiny without addressing what happens to the soul between death and the resurrection.

Article X (Last Things) does not address the destiny of the unevangelized; it states only that Christ will return, the dead will be raised, and all will be judged. The prior corpus note already conceded the document 'does not itself adjudicate the question directly' — confirmed on retrieval, so the entry is removed rather than kept on a hedge.

Article II.B is entirely about the person and work of Christ (incarnation, sinlessness, atonement, resurrection, mediatorship); nothing in the Baptist Faith and Message characterizes non-Christian religions as false or demonic, and no other article addresses the subject.

Article XI commands making disciples of “all nations” in general terms and never mentions Jewish people or Judaism specifically anywhere in the document; the specific claim about Jewish evangelism is not addressed.
Article I addresses Scripture's inspiration, truthfulness and authority; it says nothing about interpretive method, grammatical-historical or otherwise, anywhere in the document.

Article I never mentions Bible translations; it addresses only Scripture's inspiration and authority. Baptist remains attested on this doctrine via the kjv-only position's own held_by entry (cited to Peter Ruckman, not the BF&M), so removing this entry does not orphan the tradition_overrides.baptist entry, which requires the tradition to appear in at least one of its listed positions.
